meta.title: Rescue Control — Emergency management simulator
meta.description: Run your city’s control room: dispatch vehicles, manage stations and grow your rescue network on a real map.

common.disclaimer: Rescue Control is a game. In a real emergency, call 112. Not affiliated with any emergency service or agency.

auth.pitch: A real city. Real emergencies. Every call is yours.

email.title: Enter the control room
email.subtitle: Enter your email and we’ll send you an access code. It works for both signing in and signing up.

profile.title: Welcome, Director
profile.subtitle: This is your first sign-in. Choose the name you’ll sign your duty orders with.
profile.nameHint: 3 to 24 characters: letters, numbers, spaces and . _ - ’
profile.nameInvalid: Use 3 to 24 characters: letters, numbers, spaces and . _ - ’
profile.acceptTerms: I accept the Terms of Service and have read the Privacy Policy

profile.marketing: I’d like to receive game news and updates by email

location.title: Where are you reporting for duty, {name}?
location.subtitle: Choose the municipality where you’ll open your first control room. The map, roads and distances are the real ones.
location.placeholder: Search for a municipality, e.g. Pescara
location.hint: Type at least two letters to search.
location.emptyHint: Check the name or try a nearby municipality.

sites.title: Choose your first station in {location}
sites.subtitle: Three locations, three play styles. Compare coverage and response times: you can open more stations later.

hint.CENTRAL: You get almost anywhere fast, but there’s little room to grow.
hint.BALANCED: A good trade-off between response times and room for new vehicles. Recommended.
hint.PERIPHERAL: Plenty of room and low growth costs, but longer runs to the centre.

creating.title: Opening your control room…
creating.body: We’re setting up the station, your first vehicle and the crew in {location}.

WELCOME.title: Welcome to the control room, Director
WELCOME.body: The first call has come in. In a few steps you’ll see how an emergency is handled from start to finish.

SELECT_INCIDENT.title: Open the call
SELECT_INCIDENT.body: Active emergencies are always in this queue, sorted by urgency. Select it to read what’s happening.

DISPATCH.title: Dispatch the vehicles
DISPATCH.body: The bars show what’s needed. The control room suggests the best vehicles: one tap and they’re on their way. You can always pick by hand.

WATCH_ARRIVAL.title: The vehicle is en route
WATCH_ARRIVAL.body: Follow it on the map: on arrival the operation starts and progresses according to how well the vehicles on scene cover the needs.

OUTCOME.title: Mission complete
OUTCOME.body: Read the report: reward, costs and experience.

BUY_VEHICLE.title: Grow your fleet
BUY_VEHICLE.body: With the reward you can afford a second vehicle. Open the Shop and choose one: two vehicles mean two emergencies handled at once.

settings.title: Settings
settings.soundHint: An alert for new emergencies and for dispatch confirmation.
settings.reducedMotionHint: Turns off pulses and transitions; vehicles update in steps.
settings.deleteBody: This request starts the permanent deletion of your account and career. You’ll be signed out immediately. It can’t be undone after the cooling-off period.

TRASH_FIRE.title: Bin fire
TRASH_FIRE.report: There are some bins on fire at {address}, and the flames are getting close to the parked cars.

CAR_FIRE.title: Car on fire
CAR_FIRE.report: There’s a car on fire at {address}! Black smoke’s pouring out of the bonnet, there’s nobody inside.

APARTMENT_FIRE.title: Flat fire
APARTMENT_FIRE.report: There’s smoke coming out of a third-floor window at {address}. I think there are still people in the building.

ELEVATOR_RESCUE.title: People stuck in a lift
ELEVATOR_RESCUE.report: There are two of us stuck in a lift between floors, at {address}. One of us is claustrophobic.

FALLEN_TREE.title: Tree down on the road
FALLEN_TREE.report: A big tree’s come down at {address}, it’s blocking the whole road.

FLOODED_BASEMENT.title: Flooded basement
FLOODED_BASEMENT.report: The basement’s flooded at {address} and the water’s still rising, the fuse box is down there.

ROAD_ACCIDENT.title: Road traffic collision
ROAD_ACCIDENT.report: Two cars have crashed at {address}. Everyone got out on their own but there’s fluid all over the road.

ROAD_ACCIDENT_TRAPPED.title: Collision with person trapped
ROAD_ACCIDENT_TRAPPED.report: A car’s rolled over at {address}. The driver’s conscious but can’t get out!

GAS_LEAK.title: Gas leak
GAS_LEAK.report: There’s a strong smell of gas in the stairwell of the building at {address}.

MEDICAL_MINOR.title: Person taken ill
MEDICAL_MINOR.report: Someone’s been taken ill at {address}. They’re conscious but very pale.

FALL_INJURY.title: Fall with injury
FALL_INJURY.report: A man’s fallen off a ladder at {address}, his leg’s really hurting and he can’t get up.

CARDIAC_ARREST.title: Cardiac arrest
CARDIAC_ARREST.report: Come quick! A man’s collapsed at {address}, he’s not responding and he’s not breathing!

config.title: Configuration versions
config.subtitle: Game balance lives in versioned configurations: a draft only becomes active once it’s published.

design.title: Design system
design.intro: A dark control-room theme derived from the logo: midnight-blue surfaces, brand red, silver text. States never rely on colour alone: every state also has an icon, a label or a pattern.
design.sheetBody: Drag the handle or press it to switch between the three heights.

dialog.title: Dialog title
dialog.body: On a phone the dialog slides up from the bottom, within thumb’s reach.

empty.title: Nothing to show
empty.body: Empty states always explain what happens next.
